신서고 2-2 중간 · YBM(박준언)
주제찾기
1 1번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Picture a city district sliding into ruin after the economy collapses. Shops shut down, landlords walk away, and empty buildings line every block. Winter arrives with no heat, and the only residents left are those too poor to leave. Jobs disappear, gangs multiply, and fighting among the young becomes ordinary. Then a gang known for feeding and treating its neighbors decides that violence must end. Its members urge other young people to unite and rebuild the community instead. Gang leaders across the district agree to a peace treaty and abandon their weapons. Out of that fragile peace in the Bronx of the early 1970s, hip-hop was born.
①the birth of hip-hop out of a community's choice to end violence
②the economic policies that caused American cities to decline
③the difficulty of enforcing peace treaties between rival groups
④the role of free meal programs in reducing urban poverty
⑤the musical techniques that made early hip-hop distinctive
2 2번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Once the peace treaty held, rival gangs began throwing parties with one another instead of fighting. Empty lots and deserted buildings turned into stages for gatherings called block parties. Out of those gatherings grew a lively youth movement that people came to call hip-hop culture. It rested on four pillars, and it pushed street violence aside in favor of music, dance, art, and style. The parties thrown by DJ Kool Herc drew the biggest crowds of all. By running two copies of one record on two turntables, he stretched the drum passage dancers loved most. That stretched passage gave rise to circles of dancers who competed to show what they could do. It also gave rise to the rhymed shouting over instrumentals that later became a role of its own.
①how hip-hop culture took shape at Bronx block parties
②the technical challenge of operating two turntables at once
③the reasons street gangs finally stopped fighting in New York
④the contribution of graffiti artists to urban neighborhoods
⑤the worldwide commercial success of modern rap music
Terra Nova · 변형문제 1
신서고 2-2 중간 · YBM(박준언)
주제찾기
3 3번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Where the word hip-hop came from is something no one can prove. Still, the story most often told places its first use at a block party. A young man there was days away from reporting to the army. His close friend, who was running the party as MC, decided to tease him about it. Marching across the stage to the beat like a drill instructor, he chanted the syllables hip-hop again and again. The crowd was delighted, and other MCs soon built their own playful lines out of the same sounds. Those lines hardened into a regular feature of rap and reached the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album. With that record, the music, the dancing, and the name itself travelled far beyond the Bronx.
①how a playful party chant turned into the name of a culture
②the strict training methods used by American military instructors
③the recording techniques behind the first hip-hop album of 1979
④the difficulty of tracing the origins of English slang words
⑤the reasons young men in the Bronx chose to join the army
4 4번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
In its earliest days, rap was little more than shouting used to keep a party alive. The words praised the skill of the DJ or the rapper and invited everyone to enjoy the night. During the 1980s, however, the content of those words changed in a decisive way. In 1982 a group called Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five released a song that described the cruelty of ghetto life in detail. From that point on, rappers used their verses to attack unfairness rather than simply to entertain. Later a second change appeared, one best captured by the single word respect. Rappers honored the founders who had built a culture out of almost nothing. They also claimed that same dignity for themselves and for the listeners who had survived alongside them.
①how the content of rap lyrics moved from boasting to social criticism and respect
②the technical training that turns an ordinary teenager into a skilled DJ
③the commercial strategies that made rap records sell in the 1980s
④the daily hardships faced by children growing up in American ghettos
⑤the influence of dance rhythms on the popularity of party music
Terra Nova · 변형문제 2
신서고 2-2 중간 · YBM(박준언)
주제찾기
5 5번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
On May 16th, 2001, a document called The HipHop Declaration of Peace was handed to the United Nations. By accepting it, the world formally treated hip-hop as an international culture of peace. The declaration also called attention to the genre's first purpose, which was to calm the violence of the Bronx. In this way it showed that hip-hop's history had earned worldwide respect. A second milestone arrived in 2018, when the rapper Kendrick Lamar received a Pulitzer Prize for Music. That award placed a music once confined to the underground beside forms as established as classical composition. Today listeners treat hip-hop as a way to speak for themselves, to resist unfairness, and to press for social change. Because that appeal keeps widening, hip-hop remains a phenomenon on a global scale.
①hip-hop's growth into a globally recognized art form and voice for change
②the procedures by which the United Nations approves cultural documents
③the reasons classical music continues to dominate serious concert halls
④the history of gang violence in the Bronx during the 1970s
⑤the difficulty of judging popular music by traditional artistic standards

6 1번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Imagine a neighborhood that falls apart after a severe recession. Businesses close, owners flee, and abandoned buildings stand without heat through the winter. Only families who cannot afford to move stay behind. Unemployment climbs, gangs spread, and violence becomes part of daily life. One respected gang, known for its free meals and medical care, chooses to stop fighting. It persuades other young people to unite and build something better together. Leaders from across the area sign a treaty and vow never to settle disputes by force again. That decision turned the Bronx into the birthplace of a new culture of peace.
①공동체가 폭력을 끝내기로 한 선택이 새로운 문화를 탄생시켰다.
②경제 침체를 막으려면 정부의 신속한 개입이 필요하다.
③갱단의 폭력은 결국 더 큰 폭력으로만 해결될 수 있다.
④도시의 빈곤은 주민들의 이주를 통해서만 완화된다.
⑤음악은 청소년의 일탈을 예방하는 가장 효과적인 수단이다.
7 2번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
With the fighting over, the gangs that had once attacked each other started celebrating side by side. Vacant parking lots and empty buildings became the venues for events known as block parties. What came out of them was an energetic youth movement built on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. In place of gang violence, the neighborhood now had music, dance, art, and style. DJ Kool Herc, later called the founding father of hip-hop, hosted the parties everyone wanted to attend. His trick of switching between two identical records lengthened the drum break that dancers waited for. Because the break never had to end, people formed circles and turned dancing into a contest of skill. Meanwhile the rhymed shouting DJs used to fire up the crowd grew into a separate job of its own.
①블록 파티에서 시작된 힙합 문화가 폭력을 대신하며 여러 갈래로 자라났다.
②새로운 음향 장비의 발명이 대중음악의 흐름을 완전히 바꾸어 놓았다.
③갱단의 폭력은 결국 더 강력한 단속을 통해서만 줄어들 수 있었다.
④청소년에게는 무엇보다 안전한 실내 공연장을 마련해 주어야 한다.
⑤그래피티는 도시 미관을 해치기보다 지역 정체성을 강화하는 예술이다.
Terra Nova · 변형문제 4

요지찾기
8 3번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Nobody can say for certain where the word hip-hop first came from. What people repeat is that it was heard for the first time at a block party. One guest at that party was about to leave for military service. The MC, a close friend of his, teased him that his free days were finished. He strode across the stage to the beat like an army instructor, chanting hip-hop over and over. The audience loved the joke, and other MCs began testing similar lines of their own. Before long such lines were a standard part of rap and appeared in Rapper's Delight in 1979. The album succeeded at once, and the new music and dancing spread very quickly.
①장난으로 시작된 구호가 랩의 표준이 되어 문화와 함께 퍼져 나갔다.
②힙합의 정확한 어원을 밝히는 일이 음악사의 가장 시급한 과제이다.
③최초의 힙합 앨범은 대중의 외면을 받아 상업적으로 실패하였다.
④군대 문화가 미국 대중음악의 리듬 형성에 결정적 영향을 주었다.
⑤가사보다는 연주 실력이 힙합 음악의 성패를 좌우한다.
9 4번 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
Rap began as party talk, focused on fun and on showing off the DJ's or the rapper's ability. That focus shifted sharply once hip-hop grew popular in the 1980s. A 1982 record called The Message spelled out the harsh truths of ghetto life. It told of a boy who was born there and had to live and die as a second-class citizen. After that song, hip-hop carried a tradition of speaking out against injustice. Its rhythm still moved bodies, so listeners took in the message while they danced. A further attitude then grew in the lyrics, one that can be summed up as respect. Rappers honored the pioneers and, through them, honored their own worth as well.
①힙합의 가사는 오락에서 사회 비판과 존경의 언어로 발전해 왔다.
②대중음악의 상업적 성공은 리듬의 완성도에 달려 있다.
③빈민가의 문제는 음악이 아니라 정책으로만 해결될 수 있다.
④예술가는 사회 문제를 다룰 때 개인적 감정을 배제해야 한다.
⑤춤추기 좋은 음악일수록 메시지를 담기 어려워진다.

A peace declaration for hip-hop reached the United Nations on May 16th, 2001. With that step, hip-hop was officially named an international culture of peace. The paper reminded readers that the music had first tried to bring calm to the Bronx. Recognizing that mission meant recognizing the genre's whole history. In 2018 Kendrick Lamar won a Pulitzer Prize for Music, and the news carried similar weight. Music that had begun underground now stood beside classical work as a major art form. People today use hip-hop to express themselves, oppose injustice, and stay connected to one another. Its appeal keeps growing, and the genre continues to spread across the world.
①언더그라운드에서 출발한 힙합은 이제 세계적으로 인정받는 주요 예술이자 표현의 수단이 되었다.
②국제기구의 인증을 받아야만 대중음악은 예술로 대접받을 수 있다.
③클래식 음악의 권위는 어떤 대중 장르로도 대체될 수 없다.
④음악상은 예술가의 창작 자유를 제한하는 부작용을 낳는다.
⑤지역 문화가 세계로 퍼지면 본래의 정신은 대개 사라진다.

11 1번 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
In the early 1970s the South Bronx was collapsing under an economic downturn. Storefronts were boarded, owners had vanished, and whole rows of buildings stood empty. There was no heating in winter, and only the poorest families remained. Gang violence among young people had become an everyday event. A gang called the Ghetto Brothers, respected for its free meal and medical programs, decided to stop fighting. Its members argued that unity, not violence, could make the town worth living in. Gang leaders from across the area signed a peace treaty and renounced violence. In that space of peace, hip-hop emerged as the voice of a new culture.
①From Broken Streets to a Culture of Peace
②How Recessions Destroy American Cities
③The Rules That Every Street Gang Follows
④Winter in the Bronx: A Housing Crisis
⑤Why Peace Treaties Usually Fail
12 2번 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
After the treaty, former enemies in the Bronx began holding parties together in the open air. Abandoned lots and empty buildings hosted the events people called block parties. From these parties came hip-hop culture, resting on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. DJ Kool Herc, regarded as the founding father of hip-hop, hosted the most popular of them all. At his sister's birthday party in August 1973 he tried something no one had done before. Playing two copies of one record on two decks, he switched back and forth to stretch the drum break. Dancers no longer had to stop, so they made circles and turned the break into a stage of their own. DJs rhyming over the instrumental parts eventually handed that job to a friend, and MCing was born.
①One Stretched Break, Three New Art Forms
②The Hidden Cost of Running Two Turntables
③Why Block Parties Were Banned in the Bronx
④Graffiti: The Forgotten Pillar of Hip-Hop
⑤How Rap Conquered the Global Music Market

After the recession, the district filled with empty buildings and cold apartments. Unemployment was high and gang violence had become an everyday thing. Then a gang respected for its free meals and medical care made an unexpected choice. Rather than fight on, its members urged young people to unite and rebuild. In other words, the community discovered that . That discovery cleared the ground on which hip-hop culture would grow.

The block parties that followed the treaty drew crowds into empty lots all over the Bronx. The parties everyone talked about were the ones hosted by DJ Kool Herc. In August 1973 he set up two turntables and loaded the same record onto both of them. By switching from one deck to the other, he made the drum break run on and on. Dancers who had once waited through the quiet parts now had a stage that never closed. They gathered in circles, and each of them stepped in to show what only he or she could do. In short, Herc's technique turned a few seconds of drumming into . From that space came the B-Boys, the B-Girls, and the whole street battle culture.

The MC, his closest friend, marched across the stage like a drill instructor to the beat. As he marched he chanted the syllables hip-hop, and the crowd roared with delight. Other MCs heard about it and began testing lines built from the same nonsense sounds. Those lines soon appeared in the lyrics of the first recorded hip-hop album. In other words, the name of a whole culture began as . Nobody planned it, yet the word travelled with the music wherever it went.

Early rap verses were party chants about having fun and about the DJ's skill. That changed in 1982, when The Message described the cruelty of ghetto life in detail. Afterward hip-hop attacked injustice, yet its beat still made listeners dance. A second change followed, and it can be summed up in the word respect. Rappers treated the early artists as heroes who made something from nothing. They also insisted that they and their audience had survived the same hardships. In short, the respect celebrated in hip-hop lyrics is . That double meaning explains why the idea cannot be emphasized strongly enough.

The exact origin of the word hip-hop is unknown, but the usual story points to a block party. A young man there was about to leave for the army. His friend, the MC, teased him that his free days were finished. He marched across the stage like a drill instructor, chanting hip-hop to the beat. The crowd loved the joke, and other MCs tried out lines of their own. Those lines became a standard part of rap and reached the lyrics of Rapper's Delight (1979). The album was an immediate success, and the new music and dancing spread very fast. When a police officer asked why violence had fallen in 1980s New York, a boy answered that people were dancing.

Its beat still made people dance, so the message traveled with the rhythm. A further attitude, summed up as respect, later entered the lyrics. Rappers admired the pioneers who had built a culture out of almost nothing. They claimed that same worth for themselves and for the listeners who had survived with them.

A hip-hop peace declaration was presented to the United Nations in May 2001. It officially recognized the genre as an international culture of peace. Today people use hip-hop to express themselves, resist injustice, and connect with others. Its widening appeal keeps the genre a global phenomenon.

Imagine an urban area that is fast becoming a slum after an economic recession. Businesses close their doors and building owners have left. The area is full of abandoned buildings. There is no heating even in winter. Only those who can't afford to move out remain. Unemployment is high, many gangs emerge, and gang violence between young people becomes an everyday thing. Despair is on every street corner. One day, however, a gang called the Ghetto Brothers, which is respected because of its free meal and medical care programs, decides to stop fighting and instead persuade young people to unite and create a better community. They suggest a peace treaty. "This is for peace, men. The violence took away our brothers. We're not gangsters anymore. We've got to make this town a better place to live." Thanks to these new voices, gang leaders from all over the area sign the treaty. Never again will they use violence to solve their disputes. This is the Bronx in the New York of the early 1970s, where hip-hop music was born as a major part of a new culture of peace created by African Americans and immigrants. The story of hip-hop, now one of the world's most dominant music genres, is a fascinating one. Let's explore it.
The Ghetto Brothers were respected because of their free meal and medical care programs, so their call for peace carried real among other gangs.

Terra Nova · 변형문제 34
신서고 2-2 중간 · YBM(박준언)
서술형 (본문 제시)
64 2번 빈칸 완성
본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
After the peace treaty, the gangs that had fought one another started partying together. Abandoned buildings and parking lots were used for events called block parties. What eventually emerged from these parties? A vibrant youth movement called hip-hop culture, based on DJing, breakdancing, MCing, and graffiti. It replaced gang violence with music, dance, art, and style. The most popular block parties were those hosted by DJ Kool Herc, who is regarded as the founding father of hip-hop. Herc's party for his sister's birthday in August 1973 is now known as the birthplace of hip-hop music because of his new DJ technique. At this party, using two turntables at the same time, Herc played two copies of the same record and then switched between them to extend the drum section known as the break. No longer did people have to stop dancing at the end of the record while the DJ changed the LP disc. Kool Herc's style of DJing quickly became influential in the rise of hip-hop music and breakdancing. The break section became the most anticipated part of a song. People would form dancer circles and use the break to show off their individual dancing skills. Kool Herc named the people dancing to his music B-Boys and B-Girls, short for Break-Boys and Break-Girls. These people began to dance in groups in the streets and build a street dance battle culture. DJs like Kool Herc would speak in rhythm and rhyme over instrumental parts of songs to excite the crowd. They would shout phrases like "To the beat" and "You don't stop!" This was the beginning of rapping or MCing. When DJs couldn't do both DJing and rhythmic shouting at the same time, they asked a friend to take the role of addressing the audience, that is, of the Master of Ceremonies or MC, at their parties. This separate role became MCing.
Because Herc used two turntables to make the drum last longer, dancers could keep moving and later formed circles to show off their skills.

본문의 내용에 맞게 빈칸에 알맞은 한 단어를 쓰시오.
Rap lyrics, which started as the party chants of early hip-hop, typically focused on having a good time together and boasting about the ability of the DJ or the rapper. However, a significant shift occurred during the rise of hip-hop music in the 1980s. Most importantly, the appearance of The Message by the group Grandmaster Flash and Furious Five in 1982 was groundbreaking. This song's powerful lyrics detailed the harsh realities of life in the ghetto, including the sad story of a boy who was born there and had to live and die as a second-class citizen. With this song, hip-hop, whose original aim was creating peace through partying, started a new tradition of social criticism against injustice. The Message became one of the most influential rap singles of all time, and was followed by many hip-hop songs that confronted racial discrimination in the 1980s and 1990s. At the same time, their music with its rhythmic beat and rapping made people move or dance. People heard the social message while moving to the beat. Also, a new attitude gradually emerged in hip-hop lyrics, which can be summarized as "respect." Hip-hop music began to be a way to express respect for one another, and particularly for hip-hop pioneers. For rappers, the pioneers are heroes who overcame hardship and injustice and went on to create new music and culture. Therefore, many hip-hoppers agree that they cannot have too much respect for these heroes. The phrase "something from nothing," often used to summarize the genre's history, is also an expression of admiration for early hip-hoppers, who developed a new culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources. Rappers also proudly expressed their feeling that they, too, and perhaps the audience, had suffered and survived in a similar way to the pioneers. This is why the message of respect is about both self-worth and respect for others. The importance of the idea of respect in hip-hop cannot be emphasized strongly enough.
Because early hip-hoppers built a whole culture in the ghetto despite very limited resources, their history is often summarized by the phrase "something from ."
